archetype.name: Dual-Threat (rhythm passer in development)
archetype.definition: A second-year starter whose floor comes from designed runs and scrambles, and who in his brief 2026 sample paired that with a quicker, more on-time short-to-intermediate passing game than he showed as a rookie.

report.headline: One sharp opener against a bad defense, then injured reserve; nothing is settled.
report.take:
Dart's 2026 is really one game. He went 23-of-29 for 230 yards and three touchdowns against Dallas, whose defense now ranks 31st by EPA. He added 54 rushing yards on 11 carries. A week later at the Rams, who rank 4th, he played 12% of the snaps and threw five passes. He has not started since: Jameis Winston started Weeks 3 and 4, Dart sat out practice in Week 3, and he is now on injured reserve and listed as QB3. The dossier doesn't say what the injury is or when he is due back, so his season line comes with a large asterisk.

Within those 38 dropbacks, the process changed in ways worth noting. His time to throw fell from 2.82 seconds as a rookie to 2.64. His aggressiveness rose from 13% to about 17%. He was surgical underneath and in the middle: 13 of 14 on throws of 0-9 air yards and 0.567 EPA per play there, plus 1.167 EPA per play on intermediate throws. His tracking CPOE was +10.9. As a rookie his CPOE was roughly zero and ranked 36th of 65, so this is either real growth in timing or one great afternoon against a defense that was beaten all year. With this sample I'd lean toward the second, and I'd credit the shorter time to throw as the one piece that could be real.

What has always been real is the running. He ran for 487 yards as a rookie, 3rd among 65 qualifiers. This year his six designed runs averaged 8.17 yards, every one was a success, and none was stuffed. That is his floor, and it shows up in fantasy even when the passing is ordinary. The flip side has also carried over: he took a sack on a third of his pressures, after ranking 45th of 64 in pressure-to-sack rate in 2025. That is partly the cost of a quarterback who looks to extend plays. The two scrambles this season produced 10 yards and no first downs, so the extending isn't yet paying for the sacks.

The numbers also hide some red-zone and third-down luck. He was 7-for-7 with three touchdowns inside the 20 and converted 8 of 9 third downs. Those rates will come down. Everything beyond 20 air yards failed: 0 for 3. When he returns, expect a mobile, quick-game starter in a run-heavy offense (the Giants' pass rate over expected ranks 30th), not a quarterback leading the league in EPA.

strengths.title: Designed runs as a floor
strengths.body: His legs are the most durable part of his profile. He finished 3rd in rushing yards among quarterbacks as a rookie, and this year his designed runs were all successful and a third of them went for explosive gains. Six carries is a small sample, but the skill matches his rookie season, so it should hold whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Quicker, on-time underneath game
strengths.body: He got the ball out faster than he did as a rookie and completed nearly everything short. Tracking CPOE was strongly positive after a flat 2025. The faster release is a process change that could stick, but the accuracy spike came almost entirely against the league's 31st-ranked defense.

strengths.title: Isaiah Likely over the middle
strengths.body: His tight end was the most productive target per look, and middle-of-the-field throws were his best area. That connection is a sensible place for the offense to restart when Dart returns, though nine targets is only a hint.

concerns.title: Injured reserve, now QB3
concerns.body: The biggest issue is availability, not skill. He left Week 2 after 12% of the snaps, has not started since, sits on injured reserve and is listed third on the depth chart. There is no expected return date in the dossier. Even once healthy, he would have to win the job back from Winston.

concerns.title: Sacks on pressure persist
concerns.body: He converted a third of his pressures into sacks, and his rookie rate ranked near the bottom of the league. That is a career trait tied to holding the ball to create. Two scrambles for 10 yards and no first downs don't yet justify the cost. He also had one turnover-worthy fumble with no interceptions, which points to ball security under duress as the thing to watch.

concerns.title: Inflated by opponent and red-zone luck
concerns.body: His league-best EPA per dropback came mostly against Dallas. A perfect red zone and an 89% third-down conversion rate are hot streaks, not baselines. The deep game went 0-for-3, and as a rookie his efficiency sat in the middle of the league.

trend.note: He went from a 26.6-point opener against Dallas to 12% of the snaps at the Rams. He then lost the starting job to Winston for Weeks 3-4 and landed on injured reserve.

nextGame.headline: On injured reserve; Washington is Winston's matchup, not his
nextGame.body:
Dart is on injured reserve and listed as QB3, so he isn't expected to play at Washington. On paper, the matchup would suit a version of him that can push the ball: Washington ranks 26th against deep passes and allows the 3rd-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Underneath, though, it ranks 5th in short-pass EPA. That is exactly where Dart did his damage in Week 1, so the setup is mixed for his style specifically.

On Washington's side, safety Nick Cross (99% of snaps) is out and Jeremy Reaves is questionable, which thins the back end. Jayden Daniels is listed out but is reportedly aiming to start, and Mariota is doubtful. Washington's quarterback situation matters more to the game script than to Dart, who would only matter here if New York activated him unexpectedly.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's leaky deep secondary
keyMatchups.body: Washington gives up big EPA on deep throws, and with Cross out it is missing a starting safety. Dart went 0-for-3 on deep shots this year, so this is the area where he would have to show something new. It is moot unless he is activated.

keyMatchups.title: Tight underneath coverage
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks among the league's best against short throws, the zone where Dart was 13-of-14. A quick-game plan would run into Washington's strength.

keyMatchups.title: Two struggling offenses
keyMatchups.body: The Giants rank 26th in offensive success rate and Washington 29th. Both run more than the situation calls for, and both have quarterback uncertainty, which points to a low-possession, grinding game.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart is designated to return from injured reserve and resumes practice, and whether Harbaugh signals he gets the job back from Winston.

restOfSeason.body:
Everything depends on when he returns and whether he reclaims the job. If he does, the rushing should carry over: around 40 rushing yards a game in rookie-like usage, plus the occasional designed-run burst. The passing should settle well below his Week 1 level. His 2025 baseline was a 6.7 yards-per-attempt passer with average accuracy, and the Giants' heavy run lean caps his volume. The quicker release is the one sign of real growth, so a modest improvement on his rookie efficiency is reasonable. The perfect red zone and near-perfect third-down rate will regress.

The projections below assume he is the starter; while he is on injured reserve, his output is zero. Fantasy value comes mainly from the rushing floor. Pressure-to-sack and a stalled deep game are the limits on his ceiling.
swingFactors: Winning the job back from Winston
Whether the faster release holds against good defenses

bets.reason: Both offenses rank in the bottom third in success rate (NYG 26th, WAS 29th), and both run more than the situation calls for. Each side has quarterback uncertainty, which supports a slow, low-scoring game. The risk is Washington's 26th-ranked deep pass defense with a starting safety out.
He is on injured reserve and listed third on the depth chart; Winston started the last two games.

confidence.note: 34 attempts, mostly one game against the 31st-ranked defense; on IR with no return date
